title: Reconstruction of a complete group from its discrete orbit functor
statement:
Let $G$ be a Hausdorff topological group whose identity has a basis of open subgroups. Assume that $G$ is compact, or complete for the two-sided uniformity: every net Cauchy for both $g_i^{-1}g_j$ and $g_ig_j^{-1}$ converges. Let $\mathcal O_G$ be the small category [def-nagata-category] with objects the left $G$-sets $G/U$ for open subgroups $U\subseteq G$, and with all $G$-equivariant maps as arrows. Give these sets the discrete topology. Write $\omega_G:\mathcal O_G\to\mathbf{Set}$ for the underlying-set functor. Topologize $\operatorname{Aut}(\omega_G)$ by pointwise convergence on all its underlying sets: basic identity neighborhoods fix finitely many specified elements of finitely many $G/U$. Then the map
$$G\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(\omega_G),\qquad g\longmapsto(s\longmapsto gs)_{G/U}$$
is an isomorphism of topological groups. Equivalently one obtains the same automorphism group and topology using the forgetful functor on all discrete continuous left $G$-sets; restriction to $\mathcal O_G$ induces this identification. Categories and sets are placed in compatible universes.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5, pp. 63–64, with Example 7.1.6 for the compact case; orbit-category formulation from the proof (the objects G/U determine a natural automorphism on all disjoint unions).
